first_impression.reaction: Googled ring styles because I'm the one buying it. I jumped to the FAQ first. Short, straight answers, each one pinned to GIA, no 'symbol of forever' rubbish. So I went back and skimmed the table and a few of the 'think twice' lines. It's a ring guide, not a sales page, and I'm fine with that. It just doesn't tell me anything about the planner, and that's what I'm actually comparing.

journey.quote: Each style gets a plain description, a "suits you if" line and a "think twice if" line, so you can shortlist two or three types of engagement rings before you sit down with a jeweller.
journey.reaction: Good. Downsides built into the format. That's what I want from anything selling me something.

journey.quote: Neither. A solitaire is clean and pairs easily with bands; a halo adds sparkle and size but needs more checks.
journey.reaction: A straight answer with a trade-off instead of 'it depends on your love story'. Gained some trust.

journey.quote: GIA says pavé is typically secure, but a lost stone is harder to replace, and it advises against pavé on the underside of the band, where friction wears hardest.
journey.reaction: Named source plus the catch. That's the stuff I'd check against GIA myself, and it would hold up.

journey.section: Key takeaways vs How to choose
journey.quote: Halo, pavé and cluster designs rely on many small stones, so book a jeweller check every six months, or at least yearly.
journey.reaction: Further down it just says 'with a check every six months'. Small thing, but which is it? I notice when the numbers don't match.

journey.section: From the ring to the wedding abroad
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, as one point of contact from first idea to the last dance.
journey.reaction: Here's the pitch. 'Anywhere in the world' with nothing behind it, then 'first idea to the last dance', which is brochure talk. And 'payments'. Whose payments, and does someone take a margin on them?

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor will take it from there, in your time zone and quoting in AUD.
journey.reaction: Quoting in AUD is useful. Quoting what, though? No fee, no model, no idea whether it's a flat fee or a cut of supplier prices.

unanswered_questions: How is the planner paid: flat fee, percentage, or commission from venues and suppliers?
Do you mark up supplier prices or take a cut from the venue?
What does a Wedded Advisor's service actually include, and what costs extra?
Is there a real wedding with the actual budget I can look at?

turn_offs_found.quote: as one point of contact from first idea to the last dance.
turn_offs_found.why: Emotional sign-off doing the job a fact should do. It's the one line in the whole piece that reads like an ad.

turn_offs_found.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world
turn_offs_found.why: Big claim, nothing to back it up. The rest of the article cites GIA for everything, then the brand claim gets no evidence at all.

would_share_with: My partner's brother, who's ring shopping, mainly for the comparison table

cta_reaction.quote: When you have a shortlist and a rough date in mind, tell us about it.
cta_reaction.why: At least it comes after the evidence, not before. But the evidence is about rings, not about you. I wouldn't enquire until I can see how you're paid and whether you take commission. One line on the fee model or a link to it would get me to click through, not to enquire straight away.

top_3_changes: In the closing section, swap 'from first idea to the last dance' for one factual line on how the Wedded Advisor is paid, or link to a page that says it (and whether supplier prices are marked up).
Back up or soften 'anywhere in the world'. Give a number, a list of regions or a link to real weddings, or cut it.
Make the jeweller-check interval the same in Key takeaways and How to choose ('every six months, or at least yearly' vs 'every six months').

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
No invented brand facts; fee model and commissions listed as unanswered, not assumed
HTML comments and image slots treated as invisible

open_questions.question: Is a fee-model link realistic for a top-of-funnel ring post, or should the fix be limited to removing the unsupported brand claim?

assumptions: Daniel is the one buying the ring, which is why he searched 'engagement ring styles' while comparing planners.
